summary: The narrator takes a pink-helmeted biker's motorcycle at gunpoint during a city-wide emergency, then rides back toward the Westside of Los Angeles through gridlocked, rioting streets. Along the way he shoots a looter who attacks his bike, and he reaches the apartment where he left Arthur. The flat is dark and empty, and Arthur is not there, leaving the narrator without a working phone to contact him.
one_line: A narrator steals a pink motorcycle at gunpoint and rides through a rioting, blacked-out Los Angeles to find his missing companion Arthur.
key_facts: The narrator swung a Mossberg shotgun at a biker wearing pink toe-shoes-style boots, on a pink bike, with a helmet that was black with pink flames.
The narrator shouted "I need your bike!" over the roar of the motorcycle's engine.
The narrator threw the biker's pink-trimmed saddlebags at her, and she did not bring her hands down fast enough to catch them.
The narrator did not steal the biker's helmet because the police had more important things to worry about right now.
The narrator intended to ride back toward LA, going the wrong way on the stopped freeway.
The 10 freeway was stopped all the way in, forcing the narrator onto the shoulder of an on ramp and into gridlocked streets.
Sirens sounded from at least three directions as the narrator rode through the city.
The narrator describes Los Angeles as not famous for the cooperation of its residents in times of trouble.
The city's streetlights were dead and silent, and every building was a blank, dark silhouette in the night.
A hoodlum swinging a crowbar through car windows ran straight at the narrator's bike, hollering a wordless berserker cry.
The narrator took his left hand off the clutch, rolled the throttle open with his right, drew a handgun, and shot the hoodlum in the head.
The narrator was two streets away from the apartment where he had left Arthur when he reached the final block.
Police lights in the final block reflected off pavement still wet from the recent rain.
The narrator arrived at the flat to find it dark and empty, and Arthur was not there.
The narrator had no working cell phone, so he had no way of contacting Arthur.
